summary: The Julia panel is built and calibrated (out/r18/panel/panel.py: run, table, sheets, user). Nine sets, six tests, 11 rules run. Blunt result: NO rule passes the panel, and NO rule passes a single set off the x-axis. twoplane passes the 4 sets of group A and fails all 5 of groups B and C (rabbit falls apart: biggest piece 97.5 %, 1,537 pieces). along passes 2 sets (airplane, cauliflower), fails basilica and San Marco on the close cut only (worst tile 1.51 and 0.71 against a line of 0.3: combs of fins), and fails all of B and C (rabbit is a lump: no ball up to 0.32 parts the three bodies, volume 3.65 x the yardstick's). oneplane (the yardstick) fails only 'truly 3D' on all 7 sets of groups A and B, as it must. Best newcomer p_tt1024 passes 2 sets (basilica at 0.26, airplane), has long needles on San Marco (3.38) and cauliflower (0.93), and falls apart on B and C exactly like twoplane. Hardest set: rabbit30 (c in no special plane): at 40 steps the solid is EMPTY for oneplane, twoplane, away, p_tt16, p_tt256, p_tt1024 (0 of 17 million points inside), wisps or crumbs for along, p_ss, p_h4, a ragged lump for p_cot; only the lathe has a solid there. All five calibration expectations of the brief hold. Weak spots I could not close: the close-cut line (0.3) sits between 0.26 and 0.42; the airplane and cauliflower 'truly 3D' tests pass at exactly the threshold for twoplane and cannot fail along; San Marco's 'bodies' test passes everything. report.md was NOT written (the harness refused a report file); the longer notes are in README.md under 'Results of this round'.

findings: MEASURED: no rule passes the panel. Sets passed out of 9: twoplane 4 (all of group A), along 2 (airplane, cauliflower), p_tt1024 2 (basilica, airplane), p_tt256 1, p_ss 1, p_cot 1, p_h4 1, p_tt16 1, oneplane 0, lathe 0, away 0.
MEASURED: no rule passes any set of group B or C (rabbit, dendrite, Siegel disc, rabbit90, rabbit30). The yardstick oneplane fails only 'truly 3D' on the three group B sets and is empty on group C.

MEASURED: calibration holds on all five known rules. oneplane fails only 'truly 3D' on 7 of 7 sets of groups A and B. twoplane passes group A and fails B and C (by falling apart: rabbit 97.5 %, Siegel 98.6 %, dendrite 92 to 95 %). The lathe fails 'truly 3D' on 8 sets (15, 11, 1 rings and 3 grooves on group A, a turn changes 0.0 %) and the tree test on the dendrite (doubling factor 4.4 = a sheet). along passes every coarse test on the basilica and fails only the close cut (1.51), and fails all of B and C. away fails the close cut on all of group A (basilica 4.91 and ribs 0.69) and is shards off the axis (rabbit: 68 % in the biggest piece with no gap allowed, 3,067 pieces).

MEASURED: rabbit30 (c in no special plane) at 40 steps: 0 of 17 million sample points inside for oneplane, twoplane, away, p_tt16, p_tt256, p_tt1024. along: volume 0.179, thickest place 0.015 (flat rabbit 0.348), 9,631 pieces, 2 % of the cut z = 0 inside (8 % at 20 steps, so it is on its way out). p_ss: crumbs (thickest 0.06 of the flat rabbit's). p_h4: 18 crumbs. p_cot: a ragged lump (thickest 0.51, hair 3.37). Lathe: exactly its rabbit, turned (0.0 % difference).

MEASURED: rabbit90 adds nothing for rules that treat the planes y = 0 and z = 0 alike: their solid differs from their rabbit's, turned a quarter turn, by 0.0 % (along, away, lathe, p_tt) or 1.6 % (twoplane). rabbit30 is the real out-of-plane test.

MEASURED: along's lumps. Rabbit: no ball up to 0.32 at the meeting point parts the three bodies (oneplane: 0.03), the ball of radius 0.1 there is 75 % full (flat disc 71 %, oneplane 49 %), volume 1.621 against oneplane's 0.444 (3.65 x). Dendrite: doubling factor 4.6 (thread 2, sheet 4, lump 8; oneplane 2.2). Siegel disc: volume only 1.37 x, so the lump test passes it; it fails on ridges (roundness of what stands off the plane 0.38) and hair (2.42).

MEASURED: newcomers. p_tt1024 close cut worst tile: basilica 0.26, San Marco 3.38, airplane 0.06, cauliflower 0.93, rabbit 2.46, Siegel 6.07; rabbit biggest piece 97.3 % (2,149 pieces); dendrite 90.9 % at 12 steps; rabbit30 empty. p_tt256 the same with basilica 0.54. They are twoplane with needles.

SEEN (sheet-for-user.png, sheets/along.png, sheets/p_tt1024.png, look/*.png): oneplane is clean everywhere it exists (balls meeting at points, a thin flat tree, a lens) but everything it has lies round the flat plane. twoplane and the p_tt rules: bodies with buds on group A; on the rabbit the balls are recognisable but broken, in a cloud of loose pieces; a bush for the dendrite; crumbs for the Siegel disc. along, p_ss, p_cot: buds in eight directions on basilica and San Marco, a barrel with eye-like dimples for the cauliflower, a ragged layered lump on every set of group B and on rabbit90. away: ribbed, then plates and shards.

SEEN (look/meetcut-all.png, point by point): on the basilica every rule shows an X at the meeting point (two bodies, one point). On San Marco the two-plane rules show an hourglass with a thick neck and oneplane is completely full: at 40 steps nothing meets at a point there. On the rabbit oneplane is a cone ending in a small blob, twoplane a saw-toothed wedge, along and the lathe a wide fused band.

SEEN (look/worst-all.png, point by point): along's hair on the basilica is a comb of parallel fins; away has dense whiskers; p_tt1024 and p_tt256 have long straight needles on San Marco and the cauliflower; twoplane and oneplane have clean lines on group A.

REASONED: for group C there is no flat set, so the 'bodies' line compares with the flat rabbit (the same c turned back into the flat plane), and 'truly 3D' takes the plane through the x-axis and c as the set's plane. This is by likeness, not a fact about those sets.

MEASURED, about the tool: verdicts are recomputed from saved numbers, so thresholds can be moved without new runs. A full run takes 10 to 25 minutes a rule on one core. Thresholds were set on the five known rules; one rule (which close-cut tile decides) was changed after seeing a round-17 rule's needles in a picture, which made the panel stricter.
disagreements: Lab picture against the iteration, group C: out/me/panel/panel-off.png shows a layered lump for along and a hollow bowl for oneplane on rabbit30 (and a bowl for oneplane on rabbit90). Point by point with the bench's exact escape test, and again with the lab-like escape radius 6, the cut z = 0 of rabbit30 at 40 steps has 2 % inside for along and nothing at all for oneplane, twoplane and away. The lab draws a surface where there is no inside. The panel judges what the iteration says; the user's lab will show something else for these sets.

Round 16 close-cut number against the picture: at the top of the middle body twoplane scored 11.6 (hairy) while the tile shows a clean line and one round bud cut off its stalk. The number counted loose bud sections as hair. Changed: only thin things count (what a 3-pixel opening removes) and the top of a body is never the skin point.

Bench rib number against the picture, off the basilica: twoplane on San Marco scored 1.00 ('ribbed', line 0.45) while the cut across (look/across.png) is a smooth disc with buds. At 40 steps San Marco's buds sit on fat necks and the measure reads them as grooves. Changed: ribs are judged on the basilica only and printed elsewhere.

'Thickest place' against the picture: along's rabbit scored 1.00 x the flat set's (not a lump) while the picture is one lump. The lump is layered and no bigger ball fits in it. Changed: volume against the yardstick added (3.65 x).

'Third worst tile decides' against the picture: it passed p_tt1024 on the cauliflower (0.93, 0.61, then 0.15) where two tiles show a long needle, and away on the cauliflower (0.42, 0.30, 0.26) where the skin is a saw edge. Changed: the worst tile decides.

Panel against round 17's close cut: p_tt256 on the basilica is 0.21 there (pass) and 0.54 here (fail). Same rule, same measure idea, different skin points. Neither is wrong; a skin is being sampled at two or three places.

Numbers against the eye on along's airplane and cauliflower: the panel passes both outright. The rough pictures show a ball with specks and a barrel with dimples, and the orchestrator called them 'unclear' and 'a rounded barrel'. I cannot say from pictures that these should pass; the tests there are too weak to fail a two-plane rule.

Turn test against the lathe off the axis: the lathe's rabbit is not spun about the x-axis (a turn changes 56 % of it), so 'rings by turning' catches the lathe only on group A. Off the axis it fails because nothing round stands off the plane, and on the dendrite its 'truly 3D' line passes while the tree test fails it as sheets.

The task asked for out/r18/panel/report.md and the harness refused to let a subagent write a report file. I did not work round the refusal. The longer notes are in README.md ('Results of this round', 'Where a measure disagreed with a picture and was changed', 'Limits') and in this return.

The four rules that passed the bench's eight tests but failed round 17's close cut (p_ss, p_cot, p_h4, p_tt16) were run on all nine sets, but their rib numbers were not computed and their close-cut tiles and sheets were not looked at.
Sheets of oneplane, twoplane, lathe, away and p_tt256 were not looked at as whole sheets, and look/front-all.png not at all.

risks: The close-cut line 0.3 is narrow: passes seen up to 0.26 (p_tt1024 basilica) and 0.25 (twoplane San Marco), fails from 0.32 (p_ss and p_cot airplane) and 0.42 (away cauliflower). Twelve tiles at two skin points in two half-planes are a small sample of a skin; a rule near the line passes or fails by luck (p_tt256 basilica: 0.21 in round 17's cut, 0.54 here).

Airplane and cauliflower 'truly 3D' pass at exactly the threshold for twoplane (2 spikes; the 2 dimples at the poles). These two sets do not tell the two-plane rules apart and cannot fail along. A new rule could pass or fail them by one voxel-sized piece.

San Marco's 'bodies' test passes every rule: at 40 steps the yardstick itself is fused there (it reaches 0.47 straight up from the meeting point; the flat set 0.12), so 'meeting at a point' cannot be seen.
On the Siegel disc 'bodies' cannot fail a layered lump (along passes it at 1.37 x the yardstick's volume); only 'truly 3D' (roundness 0.38 against 0.45) and the close cut fail it there.

Several lines sit close to numbers of rules that fail anyway: roundness off the plane 0.45 (away passes at 0.48, shard solids fail at 0.43 to 0.44); thickest place 0.8 (away rabbit passes at 0.89); one piece 99.97 (p_h4 rabbit fails at 99.96, away rabbit at 99.93). The upper thickness line 1.15 was never crossed by any rule.

Everything except the cuts (cut z = 0, cut y = 0, cut through the meeting point, the airplane's neck, the close-cut tiles, the upward reach) rests on voxels at 257 a side, 0.011 to 0.013 a voxel. Hair and necks thinner than that are invisible to 'one piece', 'bodies' and 'truly 3D'.

Group C leans on the flat rabbit as the thing to compare with (reasoned), and rabbit90 is a turned copy of the rabbit for symmetric rules, so group C is in effect one set, rabbit30, on which almost everything is empty. A rule that keeps any solid body there would be new, and the panel's group C lines have never been seen to pass.

The lab's pictures and the panel disagree on group C (the lab shows surfaces where the iteration finds no inside). If the user judges group C in the lab, they will see lumps and bowls where the panel says 'empty'.
The 'worst tile decides' rule was adopted after seeing a round-17 rule's picture. It was a change towards stricter and it agrees with the pictures, but it was not made blind.
The reviewer has no report.md to read; README.md carries the notes.

summary: The panel is a sound filter for gross faults and NOT yet a sound gate for a pass. I agree with the builder's overall pass/fail on all 45 calibration cells (5 known rules x 9 sets) by eye, and my own loop reproduces its key numbers (rabbit volumes 0.444 / 0.569 / 1.622 / 1.483 for one plane / two planes / along / lathe; along at rabbit30 0.180; every close-cut number I re-ran matches to two decimals). The headline stands: no rule passes the panel, none passes a set off the x-axis. But three things are wrong with it as a gate. (1) The 'clean close up' number fails the FLAT SET ITSELF: scored on the flat plane with the panel's own tiles, the flat basilica gets 1.23 (worst 1.96), flat San Marco 0.63 (0.93), flat airplane 0.45 (0.66), all 15 of 15 tiles over the 0.3 line. It counts ordinary small buds and beaded spines as hair; it cannot tell along's real fins (1.51) from a clean budded outline (1.96). The lathe's 'clean' fails on basilica, San Marco and airplane are this artefact. (2) The close cut looks in too few places, so its verdicts near the line are luck. With 120 tiles (8 half-planes x 5 skin points x 3 widths) instead of 12: p_tt1024 on the basilica goes from 0.26 (pass) to 5.08, with 20 tiles over the line; by eye a film of loose dust at 45 degrees and slanting fins at 33.75 degrees (0.94). Its basilica pass is false: it passes 1 set (airplane), not 2. The reference rule twoplane also crosses the line: basilica 0.15 -> 0.32 (1 tile, one small bud, clean by eye), San Marco 0.25 -> 0.52 (10 tiles; a few thin slivers along the skin by eye). (3) Group C at a fixed 40 steps is a snapshot of something draining away, and no test asks whether the solid stays: along at rabbit30 has volume 1.59, 1.20, 0.78, 0.38, 0.18, 0.04, 0.009 at 10, 14, 20, 30, 40, 60, 80 steps; it is one piece (99.98 %) at 14 steps and dust at 40. One plane and two planes are truly empty there (nothing left of 2.1 million points by step 30; one plane at rabbit90 by step 14). The lab's flat picture of this set, labelled 40 iterations, shows 4.6 times more inside than the iteration has at 40 steps (area 0.92 against 0.20) and matches about 18 steps; that mismatch between what the user sees and what the panel measures is not explained. along's passes on airplane and cauliflower survived my attempts to break them (worst 0.12 and 0.13 away from its own planes), but both sets test little. report.md was not written: this harness forbids report files; everything is in this return and in out/r18/review/ (scripts, json, pictures; start with review-sheet.png).

findings: MEASURED: the builder's numbers reproduce. My own iteration loop (not the bench's) at 129 a side gives rabbit volumes 0.4445 / 0.5686 / 1.6217 / 1.4834 (one plane / two planes / along / lathe; builder 0.444 / 0.570 / 1.621 / 1.479) and along at rabbit30 0.1796 (builder 0.179). Re-running the panel's close cut on its own 12 tiles gives the builder's worst tile every time: twoplane basilica 0.15, San Marco 0.25, airplane 0.00, cauliflower 0.01; along basilica 1.51, San Marco 0.71, airplane 0.05, cauliflower 0.04; p_tt1024 basilica 0.26.

MEASURED: 'empty at rabbit30' is true and not a voxel accident. One plane: of 2.1 million start points 76,733 are left after 6 steps, 6,195 after 10, 338 after 14, 8 after 20, 0 after 30. Two planes: 34,405 / 2,697 / 223 / 8 / 0. One plane at rabbit90: 0 after 14 steps.

MEASURED: along at rabbit30 is not wisps of a solid, it is a solid draining away. At 161 a side: volume 1.59, 1.20, 0.78, 0.38, 0.18, 0.040, 0.009 at 10, 14, 20, 30, 40, 60, 80 steps (it halves about every 9 steps); biggest piece 99.99 %, 99.98 %, 99.89 %, 98.6 %, 69 % at 10, 14, 20, 30, 40 steps. For comparison along's rabbit keeps 99.8 % of its voxels from 40 to 60 steps and the lathe at rabbit30 99.7 %.

REASONED from that: the panel has no test for 'the solid stays when the steps go up'. Every group-C verdict is taken at 40 steps only. A rule that leaks slowly could be one piece and full-bodied at 40 steps and dust at 200. Add: volume at 80 steps at least 90 % of the volume at 40.

MEASURED: the lab's flat picture of along at rabbit30, labelled 40 iterations, has cream (inside) area 0.92. The same window worked point by point with the bench's rule has 0.20 at 40 steps with the lab's escape radius 64 (0.16 with the bench's radius), and 0.82 at 20 steps. Overlap with the lab's cream is best at 14 to 20 steps (0.80, 0.79) and 0.22 at 40. The rule's formula in the lab's source is the same as the bench's (read, not run). On sets that keep their inside the two agree (rabbit: overlap 0.90 to 0.94). SEEN in lab-vs-bench-rabbit30.png: a filled ragged lump on the left, dust in the same outline on the right. Why the lab shows roughly 18 steps' worth is NOT explained.

MEASURED: the 'clean close up' number fails the flat set itself. The panel's own tiles and number on the flat plane (one-plane rule at 0 degrees, which is the flat set exactly): flat basilica 1.23 at the builder's two skin points, 1.96 worst of 15; flat San Marco 0.63 and 0.93; flat airplane 0.45 and 0.66; flat cauliflower 0.12 and 0.13. For the first three, 15 of 15 tiles are over the 0.3 line. These equal the lathe's numbers in the builder's table (1.23, 0.63, 0.45, 0.12), as they must: the lathe's cut through the axis is the flat set.

SEEN in close/flat-basilica-worst6.png and review-sheet.png row A: those failing tiles are clean arcs with round buds. SEEN in row E: along's basilica has real combs of fins (scores 2.04, 1.62, 1.51, 1.47) and, on its own exact plane at 45 degrees, the clean flat outline (scores 1.96, 1.41). The number is the same for a fault and for a clean budded outline. It measures how much of the skin is small features, not hair. So the test is biased toward rules whose skin between the planes is bald, and would fail a rule that grows natural buds there, which is what the user asked for.

MEASURED and SEEN: p_tt1024's basilica pass is false. Panel's 12 tiles: worst 0.26. My 120 tiles: worst 5.08, 20 over the line. By half-plane angle the worst is 0.30 (5.6 deg), 0.76 (11.25), 0.41 (16.9), 0.28 (22.5), 0.33 (28.1), 0.94 (33.75), 0.38 (39.4), 5.08 (45). At 45 degrees, half-way between its two planes, the picture is a film of thousands of loose specks hovering over the skin; at 33.75 degrees slanting blades stick out. twoplane at 45 degrees scores 0.19, so that plane is a fair place to look.

MEASURED and SEEN: the reference rule crosses the same line when more of its skin is looked at. twoplane basilica: 1 of 120 tiles at 0.32 (a clean line with one small bud). twoplane San Marco: 10 of 120 over the line, worst 0.52, 0.48, 0.45 at 28 to 40 degrees (thin slivers lying along the skin, buds leaning on it; nearly clean by eye). With 'worst tile decides' and a line of 0.3 the reference rule would fail two of its four passes; with the panel's 12 tiles it passes. The verdicts at 0.15 to 0.52 are decided by tile choice.

MEASURED: along's two passes hold up. Airplane: 15 tiles over the line, all 15 on its own exact plane at 45 degrees (the flat airplane's beaded spines); the other 105 tiles peak at 0.12. Cauliflower: worst 0.13 of 120. along's fails are robust too: basilica 74 of 105 tiles off the 45-degree plane over the line, San Marco 58 of 105.

REASONED: which half-planes count as 'between the special planes' depends on the rule. along has four exact planes (0, 45, 90, 135 degrees: at 45 degrees the turned plane contains the point), so 22.5 is its mid angle; a two-plane rule's mid angle is 45, which the panel never cuts. A future rule with exact planes at 22.5 degrees would be scored on the flat set itself and fail for that alone.

SEEN in across-airplane.png and across-cauliflower.png (my point-by-point cuts across the x-axis): twoplane's airplane body has beaded rays in 4 strong and about 12 faint directions, along's in 8; twoplane's cauliflower is a flower with 4 deep cusps plus scallops, along's an 8-petal flower. The panel's voxel counts say 2 for all of these (2 needed). The verdict 'truly 3D: pass' agrees with the eye, but the count that decides it sees a fraction of what is there and sits exactly on its threshold.

MEASURED (builder's numbers, read): thresholds with a number close by, besides the close cut. Roundness 0.45: away passes at 0.48, shard solids fail at 0.44 and 0.43. One piece 99.97 %: away's rabbit fails at 99.930. Thinness 0.8: away's rabbit, a shard solid, passes at 0.89. Fullness of the ball at the rabbit's meeting point: along fails at 75 against an allowance of 73. Airplane spikes and cauliflower dimples: 2 against 2 for twoplane, along and every newcomer. In each case another test fails or passes the same rule safely, so no overall verdict of this round hangs on them; the close cut is the only line that decided a pass by itself.

SEEN in look/meetcut-all.png: 'the solid reaches straight up from the meeting point' is measured in the plane y = 0, which is an exact plane for every two-plane rule, so the cut there is the flat set (twoplane, lathe, away, along and p_tt1024 give the same X on the basilica). That part of the bodies test cannot fail such a rule; only the voxel ball (1.5 voxels of radius at 0.02) tests the meeting point off the planes.

REASONED: rabbit90 adds nothing for rules that treat the two planes alike (along and lathe give identical voxel counts for rabbit and rabbit90 at every step count, measured). Group C therefore has one real set, rabbit30, and on it nothing but the lathe has a solid. A second generic c near the x-axis (for example the basilica nudged off both planes) would say whether the liked basilica survives the first step away from the axis, which is what a Mandelbrot solid is made of next to its spine.

REASONED, the answer to 'can it be trusted as the gate': as a filter, yes. Falls apart, lump, rings, empty, lopsided all agree with the pictures on all 45 calibration cells. As a certificate, no, not until: (a) the close cut is cut at 8 or more half-planes including the rule's own mid angle and 5 or more skin points, and its number is replaced or set against the flat set's own score at the same zoom, so that buds do not count and fins and loose dust do; (b) a 'the solid stays' test is added and the lab-versus-iteration mismatch at rabbit30 is settled; (c) airplane spikes and cauliflower dimples are counted from point-by-point cuts across the axis; (d) San Marco's bodies line (passes everything) and the Siegel disc's lump line (passes along's terraced lump at 1.37 x) are fixed or those sets are declared skin-and-3D tests only.
disagreements: Builder vs reviewer, p_tt1024 on the basilica: builder PASS (close cut 0.26). Reviewer FAIL: 5.08 worst of 120 tiles, 20 over the 0.3 line; dust film at 45 degrees and fins at 33.75 degrees seen. So 'best newcomer passes 2 sets' should read 1 set (airplane).

Number vs picture, lathe 'clean close up' on basilica (1.23), San Marco (0.63), airplane (0.45): the number says not clean; the picture is the flat set's own outline, clean. The flat sets themselves score exactly these numbers. The builder's calibration table lists these as fails without saying the measure is wrong there.

Number vs picture, twoplane on San Marco: 0.25 on the panel's tiles (pass), 0.52 on mine (fail by the panel's own rule); by eye nearly clean with a few slivers. Same on the basilica at 0.32 for one small bud. The builder's 'twoplane passes the 4 sets of group A' is true only for the 12 tiles it cut.

Number vs picture, along on the Siegel disc 'bodies': the line passes (volume 1.37 x the yardstick, thickest place 1.00); the picture is a terraced lump. The builder says so in its limits; the overall verdict (fail on other tests) is right.

Lab picture vs iteration, along at rabbit30: the lab shows a ragged full-size lump and a flat cut with 0.92 of inside 'at 40 iterations'; the iteration at 40 steps has dust (cut area 0.20; volume 0.18 in thousands of pieces) and at 80 steps almost nothing (0.009). The lab's cream matches about 18 steps.

Lab picture vs iteration, one plane at rabbit90 and rabbit30: the lab shows a hollow bowl; the iteration has nothing inside after 14 and 30 steps. The bowl is a surface the lab draws with no solid behind it (reasoned from the measured emptiness).

Count vs picture, 'truly 3D' on airplane and cauliflower: the panel counts 2 spikes or dimples off the plane for twoplane and along; cuts across the axis show 4 to 16 rays and 4 to 8 cusps. Verdict agrees with the eye, the number does not describe what is there.

Builder's wording, along at rabbit30 'wisps (thickest place 0.015)': true at 40 steps only. At 14 steps it is a one-piece lump (99.98 %, thickest 0.10), at 80 steps 0.009 of volume. 'No lasting solid' is the accurate description.
